titulo: Health: the doctor and the pharmacy: At the doctor's

aula.titulo: Health: the doctor and the pharmacy
aula.objetivo: Name parts of the body, say what hurts and how you feel («me duele», «tengo dolor de», «tengo fiebre»), make a doctor's appointment, understand what the doctor asks you to do (usted and the imperative) and ask for medicine at the pharmacy.

blocos.titulo: Making an appointment and understanding what the doctor asks
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to make an appointment, use the polite request from lesson 29: «Quisiera pedir una cita con el médico» (I'd like to make an appointment) or «Necesito una cita para el jueves.» Ask: «¿Tiene hueco esta tarde?» (hueco = a free slot) or «¿A qué hora puedo ir?». STEP 2: doctor and patient address each other as «usted», so everything is in the third person: «¿Qué le pasa?» (What's the matter?), «¿Dónde le duele?», «¿Desde cuándo tiene fiebre?». STEP 3: instructions use the usted imperative (lesson 28): -ar verbs take «-e»; -er and -ir verbs take «-a» — the vowels swap. So: «respire hondo» (take a deep breath), «abra la boca», «tosa» (cough), «siéntese», «descanse», «beba mucha agua», «tome una pastilla», «vuelva en una semana». STEP 4: frequency is «cada» + time («cada ocho horas» = every eight hours) or «veces al día»: «dos veces al día» (twice a day), «una vez a la semana». «Cada» never changes. STEP 5: advice comes with «tiene que» or «debe» (lesson 13): «Tiene que descansar», «Debe beber agua». Also «hay que» (one has to): «Hay que esperar dos días.» STEP 6: you answer with short phrases: «Desde ayer», «Me duele aquí», «Sí, soy alérgico a la penicilina», «No, no tengo fiebre». STEP 7: false friends: «pastilla» is a pill or tablet (and a throat lozenge), «receta» is the prescription, «embarazada» means PREGNANT — not embarrassed (that's «avergonzado/a») — and «constipado» means having a cold. STEP 8: careful: here you learn to communicate, not to treat yourself. For any health question, talk to a professional.
blocos.comparacao: English speakers have the most famous false friend in Spanish here: «estoy embarazada» means "I'm pregnant", not "I'm embarrassed" (that is «tengo vergüenza» or «estoy avergonzado/a»). Also: «receta» is both the prescription and the cooking recipe, «constipado» is a cold, and the doctor uses «usted», so his imperatives end in «-e/-a» («abra», «respire»), not the «tú» forms.

tabela.paciente: Me duele la garganta y tengo tos.
tabela.traducao: What's the matter? / My throat hurts and I have a cough.
Since when have you had a fever? / Since last night.
You need to rest. / OK, thank you.

tabela.paciente: De acuerdo. ¿Puedo pedir la cita ahora?
tabela.traducao: Come back in a week. / All right. Can I make the appointment now?

erros.motivo: With «usted», the imperative of abrir is «abra».
Days of the week take no preposition — no "ON Thursday" in Spanish.
Pregnancy is a state and takes «estar».

erros.errado: Tomo dos pastillas cada de ocho horas.
erros.certo: Tomo dos pastillas cada ocho horas.
erros.motivo: «Cada» goes straight before the time, with no «de».

blocos.enunciado: Act out a dialogue alone, out loud: first make an appointment («Quisiera pedir una cita…»), then, as the patient, describe three symptoms and how long you've had them, and finally, as the doctor, give three usted instructions.
Say from memory five sentences with «me duele», «me duelen» and «tengo dolor de». Then say a symptom with «desde hace».
